positive.reasoning: Criterion A1 (traumatic event): MET — patient described experiencing overwhelming situations involving serious threats that still affect them today. Criterion B1 (re-experiencing): MET — patient reports sudden recollections of the event and physical sensations that feel like reliving the moment. Criterion B2 (avoidance of thoughts): MET — patient stated they try to avoid thoughts or reminders of the trauma. Criterion B3 (avoidance of reminders): MET — patient avoids certain places and conversations that trigger memories. Criterion C1 (inability to recall details): MET — patient finds it hard to remember specific details of the event. Criterion C2 (negative beliefs): MET — patient experiences overwhelming negative thoughts about themselves and the world. Criterion C3 (blame): NOT MET — patient indicated occasional self-blame but not constant. Criterion C4 (negative emotions): MET — patient experiences negative emotions like fear and anger, though not constantly. Criterion C5 (diminished interest): MET — patient struggles to engage in activities they once enjoyed. Criterion C6 (detachment): MET — patient feels disconnected from others. Criterion C7 (inability to feel positive emotions): MET — patient struggles to feel happiness consistently. Criterion D1 (irritability): MET — patient reports increased irritability. Criterion D2 (recklessness): MET — patient engages in more reckless behaviors. Criterion D3 (hypervigilance): MET — patient feels more on edge than usual. Criterion D4 (startle response): MET — patient reports being more easily startled. Criterion D5 (concentration): MET — patient has difficulty concentrating. Criterion D6 (sleep disturbance): MET — patient struggles with sleep. Criterion E (duration): MET — symptoms began after the traumatic event and have lasted for more than one month. Criterion F (functional impairment): MET — patient reports significant distress and interference with work and social interactions. Exclusions: NOT MET — patient denies substance use or medical conditions contributing to symptoms. Total: 14 of 20 criteria met (threshold ≥1). Diagnosis: TRUE — full criteria for PTSD are met with significant functional impairment confirmed.
